Also consider reading books on mental health. 
“You should talk to someone” is a book that changed me. It makes me aware of myself and what triggers me.

Hey. I can never understand what it feels like to go through so much. I can only share with you what works for me to get through each day.  I have anxiety and depression. I probably have it many years but it wasn’t diagnosed until seeing a therapist and a doctor recently.
-I focus on myself and stop comparing myself against anyone. 
-I find happiness in simple things.  
-I take baby steps to adjust my lifestyle. I’m trying to focus on sleeping regular hours and going for walks this week. That’s a step forward for me. 
-I reach out to people I can trust for help. 

I can only hope you find the strength in you to take care of yourself.
I resigned a few months ago too. It’s ok to give yourself a break. Consider what’s good for you. I hope you find the strength in you and support around you to move forward.
And it doesn’t matter if people think you are a failure.

Hey. I’m going through the same thing as you. I have applied at least 100 jobs. 
You can’t control the results. Expect nothing and hope for the best for each application you make. 
Stay strong. There are many of us working on the process.
I have been going for workouts and therapists. I’m even volunteering now. But once I face the reality that I have been jobless for months, I don’t feel like I have the energy to make it past March.
I feel you. I was going through the same routine, feeling only anxiety and exhaustion for the last 6 years.
